blocks.text: JEHU SON OF HANANI, PROPHET TO BAASHA AND TO JEHOSHAPHAT · TWO KINGDOMS
Jehu. He told Baasha his house would fall like Jeroboam's, and asked Jehoshaphat, “Shouldest thou help the ungodly?”
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophet
ERA
Two kingdoms 930–586 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Baasha · Elah · Jehoshaphat
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
“Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha”; Kings says it came again “by the hand of the prophet Jehu”.
THE CALL
How the word came
“Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha”; Kings says it came again “by the hand of the prophet Jehu”. 1 Kings 16:1 1 Kings 16:7
Chronicles names “the book of Jehu the son of Hanani, who is mentioned in the book of the kings of Israel”. 2 Chronicles 20:34

Scholars' viewThe same name and father are given under Baasha and under Jehoshaphat, more than thirty years apart; commentators take him to be one man (the Jewish Encyclopedia: he “must have either lived to a very great age or begun his prophetical career very young”). 1 Kings 16:1 2 Chronicles 19:2 [50][92][111]

WHAT CAME OF THE WORD
As Scripture reports it
THE WORD
SCRIPTURE REPORTS
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Hanani, his father
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
He was alive to meet Jehoshaphat, and Chronicles names his book as the record of Jehoshaphat's acts; it does not tell of his death. 2 Chronicles 19:2 2 Chronicles 20:34
TRADITION SAYS

The Latin Vulgate reads 1 Kings 16:7 as Baasha killing Jehu: “for this cause he slew him, that is to say, Jehu the son of Hanani, the prophet” (Douay-Rheims). Chronicles, which has Jehu meet Jehoshaphat later, does not fit this reading. 1 Kings 16:7 2 Chronicles 19:2 [103][50] Who says so: The Latin Vulgate (Jerome's translation), as printed in the Clementine edition, about AD 400; printed 1598
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Nadab, Jeroboam's son
Matthew Poole (1683–1685); Joseph Benson (1811–1818); the Pulpit Commentary (1880–1897)
Poole: “i.e. Nadab; who, though he be not expressed, yet is sufficiently understood”; Baasha killed Nadab (1 Kings 15:27–28). 1 Kings 16:7 1 Kings 15:27–28 [77][2][87]
Jeroboam's whole house
Abarbanel, as reported by John Gill
Gill reports that it “may refer, as Abarbinel thinks, to the whole house of Jeroboam”; he himself prefers Nadab. 1 Kings 16:7 1 Kings 15:29 [30]
Jehu the prophet
The Latin Vulgate
The Vulgate adds words that the Douay-Rheims renders “that is to say, Jehu the son of Hanani, the prophet”; the Jewish Encyclopedia calls this a gloss. 1 Kings 16:7 [103][50]

Every passage

PASSAGES · 5

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say where Jehu lived, or how he came from prophesying against Israel's king to meeting Judah's.
It does not tell of his death; the Vulgate's reading of 1 Kings 16:7 is shown under Tradition.
This Jehu is a different man from Jehu son of Nimshi, who became king of Israel (2 Kings 9:2).
